# property-testing-testo

Testo adapter for the property-testing engine: the `#[Property]` attribute,
reflection conventions, and environment overrides. Drop-in replacement for the
frozen `rasuvaeff/property-testing` 2.x — same FQCNs, same behaviour. The
engine itself (generators, shrinking, runner, corpus, state machine) is
`rasuvaeff/property-testing-core`; see its llms.txt for the full `Gen::*`
catalog and engine API.

## Install

```bash
composer require --dev rasuvaeff/property-testing-testo
```

Migrating from `rasuvaeff/property-testing` 2.x: remove it, require this
package, change no PHP code. Core `conflict`s with the old package, so a mixed
installation fails at resolution time.

## Rules

- Drop-in from 2.x: `Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Property`, `Gen`, `Assume`,
  `Classify`, all exceptions keep their FQCNs; corpora written by 2.8
  (`PROPERTY_DB`) are read as-is; seed determinism is preserved.
- Generators/examples methods must be `public static` (`public` if the body
  needs `$this`) — their only call site is reflection, and Rector's dead-code
  set deletes private ones.
- `generators` and `examples` accept a method name or callable. A string first
  resolves to a method on the property class, then to an external callable;
  non-string callables are stored as `Closure` and invoked during resolution.
  Default convention remains `<testMethod>Generators` / `<testMethod>Examples`.
- PHP 8.3+: reusable providers can be passed as
  `[Provider::class, 'method']`, `'Provider::method'`, or an invokable object
  (`new Provider()`). PHP 8.5 also allows an inline static closure and a
  first-class callable (`Provider::method(...)`).
- An attribute `seed` disables corpus replay for that property; the env
  `PROPERTY_SEED` does NOT (it only seeds properties whose attribute omits
  `seed`).
- `runs` counts successful checks. A discarded run (`Assume::that(false)`) is
  neither a failure nor a check; the discard budget is `maxDiscards`
  (default `runs * 10`), exhausting it fails with `GaveUpException`.
- The adapter aggregates per-run `TestResult` attributes (including Testo
  codecov's `CoverageResult`) onto the one result a property test reports —
  property tests participate in coverage and mutation testing.
- `auto: true` derives a generator from the property's signature for every
  parameter the provider does not cover (Gen::forParameters rules: `@param`
  psalm type wins over the native type; unreadable types throw naming the
  method and parameter). The provider becomes PARTIAL overrides. Strictly
  opt-in, never the default (bare int/float derive their full native domain).
  No PROPERTY_AUTO env variable, deliberately.
- A provider key that is not a parameter of the property is an error, with or
  without `auto` (a provider shared by properties of different arity is
  refused).
- `#[ExpectException]` on a `#[Property]` method is refused as the test's
  error: Testo's expectation interceptor sees only the aggregate
  `PropertyViolationException` (a `RuntimeException`) and would be satisfied
  by any falsification. Use `throws:` — per run: throws the class (or a
  subclass) = pass, recorded as an assertion (a body that only throws is not
  risky); returns normally = fail `Expected <class> to be thrown, but it was
  not`, shrunk like any counterexample; another class = that failure; a skip
  or an `Assume::that()` discard keep their meaning; a failed `Assert` is
  never the expected throw, and a class Testo's assertion failures are an
  instance of (`\LogicException`, `\Exception`, `\Throwable`) is refused.

- The attribute validates nothing (Testo instantiates it before the
  interceptor runs); `runs: 0`, a negative cap, `path` without `seed`, a
  non-callable `[Cls::class, 'missing']` provider, a non-Throwable `throws`
  or one a failed assertion is an instance of are reported by the interceptor as `#[Property] on "<method>" cannot be set
  up: …` — an error of that test, never an aborted pipeline.

## API

### `#[Property]` attribute (FQCN `Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Property`)

```php
#[Property(
    runs: 100,             // successful checks to complete
    seed: null,            // pin the random phase; also disables corpus replay
    generators: null,      // method name or callable; default <testMethod>Generators
    examples: null,        // method name or callable; default <testMethod>Examples
    maxShrinks: null,      // cap accepted shrink steps; 0 disables shrinking
    maxDiscards: null,     // discard budget; default runs * 10
    timeoutMs: null,       // per-run wall-clock deadline -> DeadlineExceededException
    budgetMs: null,        // whole-phase wall-clock budget -> TimeBudgetExceededException
    shrink: null,          // ShrinkMode::Full (default) | Off | Bounded
    shrinkBudgetMs: null,  // wall-clock budget for the descent; costs determinism
    phases: null,          // list<Phase>: Examples, Corpus, Random, Shrink; null = all
    derandomize: false,    // unset seed derived from the property id
    path: null,            // replay a recorded shrink descent; REQUIRES seed
    edgeCases: EdgeCases::Mixin, // None = no numeric boundary bias
    auto: false,           // derive missing generators from the signature; provider = partial overrides
    throws: null,          // class-string<Throwable> every run must throw; per-run replacement for #[ExpectException]
    exhaustive: false,     // walk the whole parameter product when every generator is Enumerable and it fits the budget
    exhaustiveBudget: 10_000,
    flakyReplays: 2,       // re-execute the minimised counterexample; a passing replay = flaky (Flaky: line); 0 = off
    searchRuns: 0,         // targeted search after the random phase for a body calling Target::maximize()/minimize()
)]
```

### Canonical test

```php
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Gen;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Property;
use Testo\Assert;
use Testo\Test;

#[Test]
final class SortPropertyTest
{
    #[Property(runs: 300)]
    public function sortIsIdempotent(array $values): void
    {
        $once = $values;
        sort($once);
        $twice = $once;
        sort($twice);

        Assert::same($twice, $once);
    }

    /** @return array<string, \Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\ArbitraryInterface> */
    public static function sortIsIdempotentGenerators(): array
    {
        return ['values' => Gen::arrayOf(Gen::int())];
    }
}
```

### Pinned examples

```php
/** @return list<array{int, int}> */
public static function additionCommutesExamples(): array
{
    return [[0, 0], [PHP_INT_MAX, 1]]; // run before the random phase, never shrunk
}
```

### Environment variables

| Variable | Accepts | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PROPERTY_RUNS` | positive int | Overrides every property's run count, including the attribute's |
| `PROPERTY_SEED` | int | Seeds every property whose attribute omits `seed`; attribute wins |
| `PROPERTY_VERBOSE` | off for `''`, `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` (case-insensitive, trimmed); anything else enables (core 0.9: only `''`/`0` disabled) | Logs each run's arguments and each accepted shrink step |
| `PROPERTY_DB` | directory path OR `redis://host[:port][/db][?prefix=key-prefix]` (`rediss://` = TLS; parsed by core `CorpusFactory`) | Regression corpus: record on falsification, replay before the random phase, prune on green replay. A DSN builds a RedisCorpus (ext-redis preferred, else predis; neither installed THROWS) — same document as the directory form, shared between CI and developers |
| `PROPERTY_PHASES` | `examples,corpus,random,shrink` (comma-separated, case-insensitive) | Stages to run; OVERRIDES the attribute; unknown name throws |
| `PROPERTY_DERANDOMIZE` | `''` = attribute wins; `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` (case-insensitive, trimmed) force off; anything else forces on (core 0.9: only `0` was falsy) | Unset seeds derived from the property id; OVERRIDES the attribute; an attribute `seed` still wins |
| `PROPERTY_PATH` | recorded `CounterExample::$path` | Replays that descent; needs the seed of that run; an attribute `path` wins |
| `PROPERTY_EDGE_CASES` | `mixin` \| `none` (case-insensitive) | Numeric boundary bias; OVERRIDES the attribute; unknown value throws |
| `PROPERTY_EXHAUSTIVE` | flag (same words as `PROPERTY_DERANDOMIZE`) | Exhaustive mode for the suite; OVERRIDES the attribute |
| `PROPERTY_SEARCH_RUNS` | non-negative integer (`0` = off) | Search budget for the suite; OVERRIDES the attribute; malformed throws |

### Adapter classes (namespace `Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Testo`)

- `PropertyInterceptor` — self-registering Testo interceptor; resolves
  reflection + env into a core `PropertyDefinition`, maps the structured
  `PropertyResult` to one Testo `TestResult`, prints the distribution report
  and discard warning (both on `Messenger::CHANNEL_STDERR` -- a STDOUT message
  is dropped by Testo's renderer below `-v`). Constructor
  `(Messenger $messenger, ?Clock $clock = null, iterable $listeners = [])`:
  `listeners` are `PropertyListener` observers of the engine's events. Wire
  them from a `PluginConfigurator` in `testo.php` (`plugins:`); a configured
  interceptor wins over the one the attribute self-registers:

  ```php
  $container->get(InterceptorCollector::class)->addInterceptor(
      $container->make(PropertyInterceptor::class, ['listeners' => [new MyListener()]]),
  );
  ```
- `TestoTrialExecutor` — runs the body through Testo's pipeline; merges every
  run's `TestResult` attributes into the aggregate result.
- `VerboseListener` — `PROPERTY_VERBOSE` output as an engine event listener;
  exception-hardened so an output bug cannot fail the run.

### Stateful testing

```php
#[Property(runs: 200)]
public function stackBehavesLikeItsModel(CommandSequence $sequence): void
{
    StateMachine::check($sequence, static fn(): Stack => new Stack());
}
```

`Gen::commands()`, the `Command` interface and `StateMachine::check()` are core
API — see the core package's llms.txt. `StateMachine::check()` throws rather
than recording Testo assertions: mark such a property `#[ExpectNoAssertions]`
or it comes back Risky.

### Examples

`examples/*.php` are `#[Property]` test cases in a Testo suite of their own:
`vendor/bin/testo --suite=Examples`.
